The post OPINION: Your product is no longer a competitive advantage appeared first on EU-Startups.
item.content:encoded:
A friend of mine runs a company that builds software for other companies. He has the same problem in most sales meetings. He shows what the system can do, the prospect leans forward and asks how it works, and my friend, who is not daft, goes slightly vague. If he explains it properly, they might go away and build it themselves.

Some of them go away and build it anyway. About a year later, a fair number rang back and asked for help.

So there is still money in knowing how to make something work. What AI has done is make the gap between a clever demo and a defensible company rather uncomfortable to look at. The tools that let your team build sophisticated software cheaply let a competitor rebuild it cheaply too, and your customers can have a go over a long weekend. The development bill has come down for everyone. That includes the people trying to put you out of business.

Your supplier has a product team too

In my previous article, I asked what would happen to a startup if its model disappeared tomorrow. There is a quieter version of that dependency. The supplier carries on answering your API calls and starts selling what you sell.

On 24 February, Anthropic released finance plugins for Claude covering equity research, investment banking, private equity and wealth management, with workflows that run across Excel and PowerPoint. If you were selling an AI equity research assistant on 23 February, you had a new slide to write for your next board meeting.

The post StrollMe bags €22 million to put more bikes, strollers and car seats into European homes appeared first on EU-Startups.
item.content:encoded:
Strollme, a German provider of children’s mobility on subscription, has secured €22 million in equity and debt financing to support their growth in its existing markets and lay the foundation for future expansion into other European countries.

Existing investors including Hanse Ventures, HGDF, JOSS and business angel Kristina Schreiner from the better ventures network are participating again, alongside new investor BMH Beteiligungs-Managementgesellschaft Hessen mbH (BMH), investing through its managed fund Hessen Kapital I. The credit facility is provided by Growth Credit Partners (GCP).

Sebastian Reichelt, co-founder and Managing Director of StrollMe, says: “This financing is a milestone for StrollMe. The equity from our existing and new investors and the credit facility from Growth Credit Partners enable us to significantly expand our fleet and offer families even more choice on subscription. We have also laid the foundation to strengthen our position in Europe step by step and in a capital-efficient way.”

StrollMe’s financing comes amid further investment in European subscription and asset-backed business models in 2026.

In the UK, London-based Raylo secured €34.5 million in equity and debt to expand its electronics subscription offering, while GIN e-bikes received €215k in fleet-backed debt to grow its bicycle rental service. In Germany, Berlin-based Everphone obtained €15 million in refinancing for its leased device fleet, while London’s equipal announced €18.84 million in equipment financing and equity.

Together with StrollMe, these announcements represent approximately €90.6 million in combined financing, including debt and refinancing facilities.

The post Pieterjan Bouten’s Entourage closes €100 million second fund after surpassing €75 million target in two weeks appeared first on EU-Startups.
item.content:encoded:
Entourage, the London-based early-stage VC firm founded by Showpad co-founder and former CEO Pieterjan Bouten, today announced the close of its €100 million second fund, just over two years after launching its first fund in 2024.

Entourage Fund II has been backed entirely by entrepreneurs, family offices and private investors, including founders behind Aikido, TechWolf and Collibra. It has surpassed its original €75 million target in just 2 weeks and has secured over €100 million in commitments before being capped at €100 million. 

“When we launched Entourage two years ago, we had a simple ambition: to back the next generation of legendary founders. We wrote the first cheques into companies like Aikido, Conveo and Lexroom. What these founders have achieved in such a short time has only strengthened our conviction in our founder-first approach. With Fund II, we’re doubling down,” said Pieterjan (PJ) Bouten, Founder and General Partner of Entourage. 

Founded in 2024 by Bouten, Entourage claims to bring a founder’s mindset and an operator’s experience to venture capital. It backs “exceptional founders” at the pre-Seed and Seed stages and invests across sectors, including AI, enterprise software, robotics, and DeepTech. 

Bouten co-founded and scaled Showpad into a global software company generating more than €89.84 million ($100 million) in annual recurring revenue. He then became an active angel investor before launching Entourage.

item.content:encoded:
VUSE XR, a Freiburg-based startup developing enterprise software for mixed reality training, today announced the closing of a €1.2 million pre-Seed financing round.

The round was led by IACD, a Düsseldorf-based business angel network, with additional participation from individual business angels.

“From an investor’s perspective, VUSE XR brings together everything we look for at this stage: an exceptional team, defensible AI-driven technology, and strong commercial traction. The company has demonstrated its ability to turn a technically demanding product into a scalable software business with considerable growth potential, further accelerated by continuous AI-powered feature enrichment,” said Markus Roithmeier, IACD member and Chairman of the VUSE XR Advisory Board.

Founded in November 2023 by cousins Niclas Matthias and Dr. Paul Matthias, VUSE XR develops the VUSE XR Hub, an enterprise software platform that enables industrial and life sciences companies to create, manage and deploy immersive mixed reality training for complex products and processes.

While mixed reality hardware has matured rapidly, producing the training content to run on it has remained expensive and difficult to scale; VUSE XR is addressing this problem. The startup replaces the traditional model of costly, agency-led custom mixed reality projects with a standardised, AI-assisted workflow that allows companies to build, update and distribute training content themselves, across products and locations.

The biggest selling point here is the ease with which VUSE XR helps enterprises to create mixed reality training content. The VUSE XR Hub works by converting existing CAD models, engineering data and product documentation into photorealistic 3D models, which users can then arrange into interactive training sequences using AI-assisted tools or drag-and-drop functionality.

The post Profitable Dutch startup Braid raises €34.13 million to help brands launch their own mobile connectivity appeared first on EU-Startups.
item.content:encoded:
Braid, a Dutch company that enables enterprises to launch their own branded mobile connectivity, has raised €34.13 million ($38 million) in a Series A funding round. The company also announced its rebrand from Next Communications.

The raise marks the company’s first external capital since it was founded in 2023 and was led by London-based Octopus Ventures. KPN Ventures, the strategic investment arm of Dutch telecom operator KPN, also participated in the round.

“The best infrastructure businesses make something complex feel effortless. Jignesh and the Braid team have taken an industry built around long negotiations and fragmented systems and created a materially simpler way for businesses to embed connectivity into the products their customers already use. We believe Braid is defining a new category in embedded connectivity and has the team, technology and ambition to become the default infrastructure layer for businesses delivering connectivity to their customers,” said Uthish Ranjan, Partner at Octopus Ventures.

Headquartered in The Hague, Braid was founded in 2023 by Jignesh Dave, Vishal Dave, and Mitesh Popat. The company operates across India, Europe, the Middle East and Africa. As part of this funding announcement, the company rebranded from Next Communications and claims to serve close to 90 enterprise customers, including major global FinTech and travel brands.

Before starting Braid, Jignesh Dave spent years in the UK and South African banking, including a stint at Lloyds, before building and running a mobile virtual network operator (MVNO) for seven years. That experience, which cost him €500k and 18 months of runway before a single SIM was sold, became the bedrock of Braid’s foundation: infrastructure beneath a connectivity business is more valuable than the SIM card itself.
